hero.h1: The incident board for the command post.
hero.lede: KP Rück turns the magnetic board in the rear command post into a digital one: incidents, crews, vehicles and equipment on one board – live on every device.
hero.ctaNote: No account – pick a role and go

alt.desktop: Incident board: columns from received to recon complete, crews on the left, equipment on the right
alt.phone: Field view on a team’s phone: its own incident site with the report, the crew and the status for the command post

fit.note: Grown out of the real operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – proven there, and developed further ever since.

tenet.quote: «When the network is gone, paper is in charge»
tenet.expl: A board that goes black in a power cut is not a command tool. So redundancy is built in at several levels – every level works without the one above it.

stages.h3: Several devices on the same state
stages.p: Tablets, projector displays and phones all hang live off the same board. If one device fails or freezes, another carries on – there is nothing to rescue and nothing to catch up on.

stages.h3: A standby box at the station
stages.p: A mini PC at the station mirrors the board continuously. If the internet goes down, it takes over: the board keeps running on the local network, with the map from your own tile server and the printer on the LAN. Once the network is back, what was run there is synced again.

The state of the board goes to the thermal printer every few minutes, the situation sheet at the push of a button. If everything fails, the last sheet becomes the board. On restart, one person transfers what was done by hand back into the app.

items.p: Columns are incident phases: cards move from left to right by drag and drop. The projector in the command post, the tablet on the table and the quartermaster’s phone all show the same state – without anybody pressing «refresh».

Whoever arrives checks themselves in with a QR code; duty times and breaks are tracked

items.h2: The team reports from its phone.
items.p: Every team sees its own incident sites: arrived, pickup, incident finished – without the radio. The recon team fills in its form with photos on its own phone; the report hangs on the right incident instead of getting lost in a group chat.
li: Field view without an account, by link and code
Requests – equipment, reinforcements, pickup – stay open until the command post has handled them

items.h2: The incident report writes itself along the way.
items.p: The incident log and the response times build up as you go and turn into a PDF. Corrections are made with new entries, not with an eraser – so the night stays on the record.

Incident report as a PDF with the response times

run.lede: KP Rück is open source and runs on a machine in your own station or in your own cloud. Incidents, crews, vehicles and equipment stay under your control. No licence fees, no vendor lock-in.

ways.p: Install Docker Desktop, double-click one file: the board runs on the computer at the station. The quickest way to your own data.
Docker Compose on a small server in your own network, with your own tile server and the printer on the LAN.
With a hosting provider of your choice. A standby box at the station can cover a network outage.

run.note: Help with installation and operation is available by arrangement – contact.

features.lede: Grown out of real events and exercises, not out of a feature list. Everything that comes from outside – alerting, GPS, printers – is optional: KP Rück also runs entirely without those connections.

sibling.line: KP Front – the sister project at the scene: situation map, site plans and SCBA monitoring, even without a network. Both receive the same alert and run independently.
sibling.cta: Take a look at KP Front

items.a: No more double bookings. No report lost in a group chat. Less radio traffic for questions that are on the board anyway. Everybody sees the same picture at the same time – and the incident report is already there when you get back, instead of the weekend after.

items.q: Which fire brigades and incidents is KP Rück for?
items.a: For militia, local, regional support and professional fire brigades – for everyday incidents, storm situations and several events at once. Wherever crews, vehicles and equipment have to be coordinated behind the lines, KP Rück plays to its strengths. As open-source software it can also be adapted for civil protection, command staffs and other emergency response organisations.

items.q: Where does the data live, and which interfaces are there?
items.a: Like KP Front, KP Rück is entirely self-hosted – on a machine at the station or in the organisation’s own cloud. Incidents, crews, vehicles and equipment live in its own database; there is no licence check and no usage tracking. External services such as online maps or address search receive only what the feature in use needs, and can be switched off. You can connect alerting systems (any dispatch system through the open interface, Divera and FireHub directly – with Divera, crew alerting too), a thermal printer on the local network and vehicle GPS positions. Every integration is optional.

The software itself costs nothing. KP Rück is open source (AGPL) – no licence, no subscription, no per-device fee. What remains are your own costs for operation, infrastructure and any external support you may need.

items.q: What does it take to run?
items.a: A small mini-PC or server at the station is enough. Setup, updates and backups require someone with Docker and command-line experience, whether in the brigade, the municipality or an IT support provider. The guide and administration area lead through the setup. We are happy to answer general questions; data and operation remain the responsibility of each fire brigade.

items.q: Is support available for installation and operation?
items.a: Yes. General questions about installation and use can be answered free of charge. KP Rück can be operated on an organisation’s own infrastructure or with a hosting or cloud provider of its choice. Support with installation, configuration, updates or operation is also available by individual agreement. More extensive support may be subject to a fee.

items.q: What happens during a power, network or device failure?
items.a: KP Rück saves the current state within the application and can restore it after a failure. The application can be operated on several devices and on an additional local instance. The current board can also be printed regularly and used as a fallback. External backups of the installation and infrastructure are the responsibility of the operating organisation.

items.q: Does KP Rück require KP Front?
items.a: No. KP Rück runs entirely on its own – with its own database, its own login and its own updates. It comes into its own alongside KP Front, the application for the front line at the incident: both take the same alarms from the dispatch system, read the same roster and classify alarms by the same keyword list, optionally with the same Divera access. Front and rear thus work from the same source data, without maintaining the alarm integration and the crew twice.

items.q: What is the local station printer for in KP Rück?
items.a: The station printer puts what matters on paper, right at the station or in the command post. KP Rück prints assignment slips for teams and drivers automatically if you wish, as soon as an incident is dispatched for the first time, or by hand at any time; the situation overview with incidents, vehicle status and crews, and the pickup list of equipment still on site, at the push of a button. As a fallback, the board can also be printed at regular intervals. What you connect is an ordinary 80 mm thermal printer (ESC/POS) on the local network – it works for any fire brigade, not just in Switzerland.

items.q: Can we adapt it to how we work?
items.a: Yes. Every brigade has its own administration area: incident types, priorities, crew, fleet and equipment lists are all configurable there, and import and export run through Excel. And because the whole code is on GitHub , everything else can be built – by you or to order.

items.q: Which languages are available for KP Rück?
items.a: The KP Rück user interface is currently available in German and French. As an open-source application, KP Rück can be extended to further languages. This requires a complete translation of the terminology and a professional review.

With the demo, without an account – pick a role and go. Then try it on an exercise; exercise mode is cleanly separated from the real thing. If it fits, the setup guide leads through installation and operation. We are happy to answer general questions; data and operation remain the responsibility of each fire brigade.

contact.p: The demo runs without an account. Do you want to use KP Rück at your fire brigade, or is something missing? Get in touch – we read everything.
contact.alt: For questions and open-ended ideas there are the GitHub discussions.

footer.origin: Born out of the operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – because on incidents we kept seeing the same sources of error: double bookings, scattered information and transcription mistakes made by hand. Every fire brigade runs its own KP Rück, with its own crew, its own vehicles and its own data.
